result.title: D'BEAST: Logged Bad Experiences as Explanation for Autonomous Driving Agents
result.summary: Reinforcement learning agents learn from mistakes, yet their decisions can be difficult to trace back to those experiences. We investigate whether a tabular agent's decisions can be explained by its bad experiences, defined as the training transitions associated with safety or task events. A fixed training log is replayed from the same initial Q-table under three conditions. FULL retains all updates, SKIP omits bad-experience updates, and NEUTRALIZE retains those updates without their event penalties. We illustrate the method on six classic Markov decision processes and evaluate it in closed-loop driving in CARLA. On the full driving task, FULL reached the goal from 33 of 40 test starts, whereas SKIP and NEUTRALIZE reached it from none, indicating that the bad experiences carry decision-relevant information. At the local level, for 47 decisions shortly before a failure of SKIP or NEUTRALIZE, removing or neutralizing a small group of bad experiences, with a median size of one, caused the trained agent to select the failing policy's action in 46 cases. For this agent, the results indicate that its decisions can be explained by its bad experiences.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 D'BEAST，从同一初始 Q 表重放固定训练日志，在保留全部更新、跳过「坏经验」更新、保留更新但去除事件惩罚三种条件下对比，考察表格型 RL 智能体的决策能否由其安全事故相关训练转移解释，并在六个经典 MDP 与 CARLA 闭环驾驶中验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「删除或中性化小规模训练转移以检验其对具体决策的因果贡献」的消融式归因，可能可供核查 LVR 中轨迹训练监督与 latent 内容贡献分配的问题；但对象为表格 RL 与自动驾驶，与 VLM 推理的直接关联尚需阅读原文评估。
